title: Go: Range
description: Use for range to iterate over slices, maps, and strings.

steps.title: Range Over Slice
steps.description: Create `fruits := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}` and use `for range` to print each fruit.
hints: Print each on its own line.

verification.failureMessage: Print each fruit from the fruits slice.

steps.title: Range Over Map (Keys)
steps.description: Create a map `ages := map[string]int{"Alice": 30, "Bob": 25}` and iterate to print only the keys.
hints: Only one variable gives you the key.

verification.failureMessage: Print all keys from the ages map.

steps.title: Range Over Map (Key, Value)
steps.description: Using the same map, iterate with both key and value, printing `"Alice: 30"` and `"Bob: 25"`.
hints: `for name, age := range ages { fmt.Println(name, age) }`

verification.failureMessage: Print all key-value pairs from the ages map.

steps.title: Range with Index
steps.description: Create `colors := []string{"red", "green", "blue"}` and use range to print `"0: red"`, `"1: green"`, `"2: blue"`.
hints: `for i, c := range colors { fmt.Printf("%d: %s\n", i, c) }`
The first variable from range is the index.

verification.test: output.includes('0: red') && output.includes('1: green') && output.includes('2: blue')
verification.failureMessage: Print '0: red', '1: green', '2: blue' using range.

steps.title: Range Over String (Runes)
steps.description: Use `for range` over `"Hello"` to print each rune and its position.
hints: `i` is the byte index, `r` is the rune value.
Print both index and rune for each character.

verification.test: output.includes('0') && output.includes('1') && output.includes('2') && output.includes('3') && output.includes('4') && output.includes('72')
verification.failureMessage: Print index and rune value for each character in 'Hello'.
